Subject: POC trial environment options and next steps

Thanks again for taking the call this morning 

 great to learn more about Acme's search summarization use case. Quick recap + proposed next steps so we stay aligned: 

Summary of requirements you shared:
- Target latency: sub-150ms on short queries (~512 tokens)
- Privacy: no customer data to persist beyond the trial; must meet Acme security checklist
- Scale: anticipated 200 concurrent users during trial window
- Evaluation goals: precision on summary tasks (ROUGE/QA evals) + cost per 1M tokens estimate

POC options we recommend (we discussed all three):
1) Hosted trial (fastest): Redwood-hosted model endpoints, easiest for getting started. Pros: immediate access, minimal infra. Cons: less network isolation.
2) Dedicated sandbox: reserved GPU pool in Redwood Dedicated with single-tenant capacity for the trial. Pros: predictable latency and throughput; can mirror production. Cons: longer lead time for capacity reservation.
3) VPC trial (hosted VPC / private control plane): customer network peering and private endpoints. Pros: best for stricter security controls. Cons: requires network config and firewall work.

Success criteria (what defines 'POC success'):
- Summary quality: >80% on our QA set and no major regressions vs. your baseline
- Latency: 95th percentile <= 250ms for targeted requests during peak load
- Integration: SDK + API calls integrated into your test harness and run by your eng team
- Cost estimate: Redwood provides per-token cost and recommended config to meet latency/cost tradeoff

Suggested timeline:
- Week 0 (this week): agree on environment option and sign mutual action plan
- Week 1: environment provisioning & network smoke tests
- Week 2: data/ev set upload and integration tests (we'll provide sample scripts)
- Week 3: full load tests + quality evaluation + calibration

Owner/contacts:
- Redwood: me (Marissa 

 
 
 sales/POC lead), Mateo (solutions engineer), David (inference eng)
- Acme: Tom (PM), Alice (eng)

Next steps I propose:
1) Please confirm preferred environment by EOD Wed (Mar 17). If "Hosted" is ok we can spin up access in <24 hours.
2) If Acme requires VPC or Dedicated sandbox, we'll share a network checklist and ETA for provisioning.
3) I'll attach the POC checklist and network requirements now.

Tom / Acme team — hi, Mateo from Redwood Solutions Eng. Quick answers and path forward below.

1) Hosted-first -> VPC migration: 
- Cache / state: KV/prefix caches and runtime transient state do not transfer between distinct runtime endpoints. You'll need a short re-warming period after cutover; we recommend a staged handoff where we run traffic split 80/20 to warm caches before switching.
- Model weights/config: same model variant across environments preserves model behavior; if you change quantization or model variant there can be small perf/quality differences.

2) Timeline / ETA: 
- Hosted access: keys + sandbox endpoints in <24 hours once we confirm the account and tests.
- VPC trial provisioning: typical lead time is 5-8 business days (network approvals and peering), faster if Acme can accept a hosted VPC (our managed option) — we can do in ~2 business days with the hosted VPC.
- Dedicated sandbox: if you want reserved GPUs we need a capacity commit sign-off; provisioning ~3-5 business days after sign-off.

3) Capacity recommendation: to support ~200 concurrent users with 512-token median requests and 95th p95 latency target, we recommend starting with a 4-GPU A100 equivalent pool with autoscale to 6 GPUs for peaks; we'll instrument continuous batching and advise batch size limits. We'll provide a config file.

4) Migration plan to minimize rework: 
- Start with Hosted for integration and acceptance tests (we'll provide a test harness and sample scripts).
- Parallel: open the VPC provisioning request. Once VPC is ready, we do traffic split + cache warm and switch to VPC for final evaluation.

5) Next steps / ownership: 
- Redwood: Mateo (solutions) and David (inference) own provisioning & config.
- Acme: Tom/Alice own network approvals and procurement.

I'll attach a short migration checklist and a minimal network ACL example. Happy to jump on a 30-min tech call to walk through the test harness tomorrow.
